subject.title: [Feature] Pre-response enforcement hooks (hard gates) for mandatory tool-call / policy rules

question: Should OpenClaw define a fail-closed pre-response gate in core, and what validator, tool-ledger, retry, fallback, audit, and plugin-trust semantics should that gate use?
rationale: Source inspection proves the current gap, but the permanent behavior changes final response delivery, config/defaults, plugin API contracts, and security expectations across harnesses.

options.title: Design a versioned response-gate API
options.body: Approve a maintainer-led design for a core/plugin response-gate contract with explicit validator authority, mandatory-tool ledger semantics, failure handling, and audit behavior.

options.title: Keep current hooks advisory
options.body: Document that current hooks support pre-tool blocking and output revision/cancellation only, while domain-specific policy packs remain plugin-owned without a hard final-response guarantee.

options.title: Split into narrower policy issues
options.body: Route tool confirmation, outbound pre-send, fake-tool text, and machine-wide policy hooks to their existing canonical issues and leave this umbrella open only for cross-cutting response-gate semantics.

recommendation.title: Design a versioned response-gate API
recommendation.body: Approve a maintainer-led design for a core/plugin response-gate contract with explicit validator authority, mandatory-tool ledger semantics, failure handling, and audit behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans security defaults, product scope, plugin API compatibility, and final-response delivery, and steipete is the strongest current routing candidate from prior review and recent adjacent history.
